messages:
chris: FYI — USW3 cluster bring-up tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Need a concise runbook for cold-start load run + autoscaler sanity checks. Target: ~200 GPUs, steady-state 75% util, p95 < 150ms. Also add cost guardrails. Who can own?

sana: I can own the runbook. Can we reuse the eu-west2 checklist as a baseline? link to old thread pls.

chris: Reuse for structure but not steps. USW3 constraints: private control plane, per-AZ egress caps, no shared NAT gateway. Need explicit KV cache priming for LM checkpoints.

ben: Proposed sequence: 1) infra bootstrap (tf) 2) smoke (10 nodes) 3) staged burn (50 -> 200) 4) 4h soak at 75% 5) autoscaler tuning + cost gating + handoff. I'll write the metric thresholds.

maya: +fail-open policy: if p95 > 300ms for >5m, route 20% to smaller quantized model. Also include a hard cost throttle: autoscaler cannot scale beyond commit without cost-approval flag.

sana: Draft runbook snippet below (will pull into docs repo). Commands to bootstrap + checks:

```
# bootstrap infra
terraform apply -var=region=us-west-3 -auto-approve
# deploy control-plane components
kubectl apply -f clusters/usw3/controlplane.yaml
# smoke: run 100 concurrent clients from loadgen
loadgen --target http://ingress.usw3.internal --concurrency 100 --duration 300s
# check GPU pool
kubectl -n gpu get pods -o wide
kubectl -n gpu top pods | sort -k3 -r | head -n 20
```

sana: Smoke checks to assert before staged burn: control-plane Ready, kube-proxy healthy, all node TLS certs present, NAT egress within quota.

chris: Note on networking: provider sets 20 Gbps egress per AZ. Partition model shards so cross-AZ traffic is minimized. Also blacklist large model downloads during burn to prevent thundering fetches.

ben: Monitoring rules I'll add:
- GPU util > 85% (5m) -> trigger scale-out recommendation
- queue length > 200 -> scale faster (reduce cool-down)
- GPU util < 30% and queue > 100 -> consider increasing batch sizes or lower min replicas
- p95 latency drift +20% over baseline (10m) -> trigger canary rollback

maya: Canary gating: 5% traffic for 30m (smoke), then 25% for 60m (burn), then 100% after soak. Must capture eval prompt set metrics at each stage.

chris: Cost controls: set budget watch via billing alerts and a throttle label on the autoscaler. Example: `autoscaler.max_override: "cost-guarded"` requires ops approval. Also include `rollback_to_model: v1.18-quant` command in runbook.

ben: Adding ops playbook snippets: emergency cap (scale-to-zero), rollback CLI, and how to flip model routing:

```
# emergency: cap scales
kubectl scale --replicas=0 deployment/gpu-serving --namespace=prod
# rollback to safe model
redwoodctl route set --service inference --model redwood-7b-quant:v1.18
```

deploy-bot: deploy status: cluster-usw3/control-plane apply started at 2025-07-12T09:05:12Z :rocket:

chris: Handoff: after successful 4h soak, ops oncall (rotation B) takes over. Required post-soak artifacts: smoke logs, prom snapshot, p95 baseline, cost delta, and a short runbook runbook-signoff.

sana: I'll draft the checklist and open a PR to docs with the runbook. Adding test owners and estimated run duration in the PR.

maya: quick note: include a step to prime KV cache with popular prefixes before load generation. Script: `kv-primer --model redwood-7b --keys /prompts/top1k.txt`

ben: Ack, I'll add automated alerts to the cluster channel and an oncall checklist for graceful degraded-mode fallback.

chris: perfect. tagging ops @oncall to confirm they can absorb handoff window 13:00-18:00 UTC. :thumbsup:

sana: ack from ops team lead, will be covered. final PR by EOD.

maya: I'll be on standby during the burn for model routing ops.

chris: Thanks team — runbook owner: sana. I'll review and we ship tomorrow morning.
